title: customer-poc-kickoff-storyboard-and-facilitation-notes
content:
Purpose and framing:
This document is a lightweight storyboard and facilitator notes for a 3-hour customer POC kickoff workshop. The goal is to align stakeholders, surface success criteria, agree on a minimal deployable slice, and leave with a clear ownership map and next-steps for a Redwood Dedicated/Private pilot. Use this for customer-facing workshops (pre-sales and early delivery) when engineering + product + customer success are present.

High-level objectives (what success looks like at the end of the session):
- Shared understanding of primary customer use case, data flow, and security constraints.
- Agreed minimal scope for a 2-week POC (models, routes, latency targets, throughput targets).
- Deployment footprint defined (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) and any gating compliance items listed.
- Concrete next steps: environment access, test dataset samples, and scheduled technical onboarding session.

Attendees (suggested):
- Customer: product manager, engineering lead, security/compliance rep, one end-user champion
- Redwood: solutions engineer (facilitator), platform engineer, customer success manager, sales/account executive (optional)

Workshop logistics:
- Duration: 3 hours (recommended breaks included)
- Tools: Zoom with breakout rooms, Miro/whiteboard, shared slide deck in advance, Jira ticket created for POC, pre-uploaded sample data (anonymized) to S3 bucket/access token ready
- Pre-reads sent 48hrs prior: one-page POC proposal, sample prompt set, network diagram template

Agenda (timeboxed storyboard):
Act 0 — Setup (15 min)
- 0:00–0:05: Welcome, introductions, roles, and read-out of objectives (Facilitator)
- 0:05–0:10: Quick customer context: 60-second problem statement from customer PM
- 0:10–0:15: Confirm workshop norms, outcomes, and parking-lot process (Facilitator)

Act 1 — Current-state & constraints (35 min)
- 0:15–0:25: Customer systems walk-through (architecture, current inference path, data residency) — customer lead speaks; facilitator probes for SLOs and security requirements
- 0:25–0:40: Rapid risk map: identify must-have constraints (data encryption, PII, network egress, regulatory redlines). Capture as a 3-column Miro board: constraint / impact / mitigation owner

Facilitator cues:
- Use concrete prompts: "Who touches the data? Where is it stored? What is the expected 95th% latency for user-facing requests?"
- If compliance folks are quiet, call out: "Is there any required audit log retention period or KMS requirement?"

Act 2 — Define Minimal POC (50 min)
- 0:40–1:00: Define the minimal deliverable: pick 1–2 critical flows and measurable success metric(s). Examples: 95th%-tile ≤ 350ms for assistant flow; relevance NDCG@10 for reranker >= 0.72. Capture evaluation approach.
- 1:00–1:10: Breakout (customer eng + Redwood eng) for 10 minutes: map request flow to Redwood runtime components (model choice, quantization, batching strategy, KV cache needs)
- 1:10–1:30: Reconvene: each breakout reports back; facilitator synthesizes model variant and deployment mode recommendation (hosted/dedicated/private).

Slide outline for the deck (speaker notes included):
- Slide 1: Title + Objectives (speak to 3 outcomes we need by EOD)
- Slide 2: Current-state diagram (ask customer to confirm live) — speaker note: draw attention to data ingress and adjacency to regulated systems
- Slide 3: Constraints & non-negotiables — speaker note: ensure security/compliance voice is captured verbatim on the slide
- Slide 4: Proposed minimal POC scope (flows, models, datasets) — speaker note: show 2-week timeline milestones
- Slide 5: Target metrics and evaluation plan — speaker note: define measurement cadence and tooling (console traces, token-level cost)
- Slide 6: Deployment proposal and options (pros/cons) — speaker note: include cost/back-of-envelope and estimated latency tiers
- Slide 7: Roles & RACI for POC delivery — speaker note: call out customer env access and Redwood deliverables
- Slide 8: Risk register and immediate mitigations — speaker note: have entry for fallback to smaller model or hosted fallback route
- Slide 9: Next steps and calendar requests (tech onboarding, data handoff)

Interactive activities and prompts:
- Rapid test-case prioritization: give customers 6 synthetic test cases, ask them to vote top 2 for the POC 
- Load-profile estimation: facilitator walks through current qps and projected peak, then plots whether Dedicated pump or Hosted burst fits better
- Security quiz: 5 quick yes/no prompts to confirm whether KMS/HSM, VPC peering, and private endpoints are required

Break guidance: schedule a 10-minute break at ~60 minutes and a 5-minute stretch at 120 minutes

Deliverables by workshop close:
- Agreed POC charter (1-pager) authored during session and owned by customer PM + SE
- Jira epic created with acceptance criteria and sample prompts/tests attached (copy link in linked_artifacts)
- Action log with owners and due dates (send within 24 hours)

Acceptance criteria templates (pick one):
- Latency-driven: 95th%-tile < 350ms for production-like traffic, success if sustained for 3 consecutive measurement windows
- Quality-driven: Evaluation on gold prompt set yields >= baseline score (provide baseline numbers) and no semantic regressions on core flows
- Integration-driven: API keys and VPC peering in place, automated smoke test completes from customer staging environment

Onboarding & environment checklist (engineering pre-reqs):
- NDA executed (if not already)
- Customer provides test data sample (anonymized) and sample prompts; S3 path or secure upload provided
- Network access: IP allowlist entries OR VPC peering details OR private endpoint config
- KMS info: customer KMS ARN for encrypted artifacts (if Private)
- Expected traffic profile and concurrency numbers
- Contact list with escalation phone/email

Common risks and facilitator mitigation scripts:
- Risk: Compliance blocker discovered late. Script: "Let's capture the specific requirement and put it on the risk log; meanwhile we propose a hosted fallback path for demoing core flows without production data."
- Risk: Customer scope creep. Script: "We will park non-critical asks in a backlog but confirm minimal slice that will be delivered in the 2-week POC; anything outside requires a new ticket and timeline."
- Risk: No test data available. Script: "We will provide a synthetic data generator template and run a smoke pass; this is not a quality guarantee but will unblock early integration tests."

Facilitator checklist (pre-work) — items to complete 48–72 hours before workshop:
- Share one-pager POC proposal and slide deck draft with customer
- Confirm attendees and their decision-making authority
- Create Jira epic and invite customer PM to the epic
- Provision demo environment (hosted token or dedicated trial cluster) and create a smoke-run notebook
- Prepare 3 synthetic prompts and 3 example metrics graphs to illustrate Console views

Post-session follow-up template (to send within 24 hours):
- Subject: "POC Kickoff recap & action log — <customer name>"
- Body: short recap of agreed scope, attached 1-pager charter, actions table with owners + due dates, link to jira epic and next calendar item (tech onboarding)

Notes on deployment recommendation heuristics (quick heuristics to pick mode):
- If data residency OR KMS/HSM required AND customer wants dedicated SLA -> Private.
- If predictable high sustained throughput > 200 qps with consistent low-latency needs and long-term commitment -> Dedicated.
- If exploratory, low QPS, or need fastest time-to-first-demo -> Hosted.

Sample action log (fill during session):
- Action: Customer to provide sample dataset (owner: Customer PM; due: +3 business days)
- Action: Redwood SE to provision demo endpoint and share credentials (owner: Priya; due: +2 business days)
- Action: Schedule technical onboarding deep-dive (owner: Redwood CSM; due: +5 business days)

Appendix (optional artifacts to attach in drive):
- Sample POC charter template (1-pager)
- Network diagram template (Visio/PNG)
- Synthetic data generator script (notebook link)
- Console screenshots showing token-level cost and latency breakdowns

Facilitator retrospection prompts (for internal use after workshop):
- What questions did the customer struggle to answer? (implies missing discovery)
- Which risks appeared underestimated?
- Did the proposed minimal slice feel deliverable in the stated timeline?
- Who on the customer side took ownership signals — call them out in the follow-up

End of document.
